method: Offered traffic A in erlangs is the busy-hour load: call attempts per hour multiplied by average holding time in seconds, divided by 3600. Erlang B models a group of n trunks with Poisson arrivals, blocked calls cleared and no retries: B(0) = 1 and B(n) = A x B(n-1) / (n + A x B(n-1)), evaluated iteratively in double precision up to 1,500 trunks, so the blocking probability for the entered trunk count is B at that index. Carried traffic is A x (1 - B) erlangs and blocked traffic is A x B. The trunk count a grade of service needs is the smallest n whose B x 100 is at or below the target blocking percentage, searched from 1 upwards; the table lists the seven trunk counts around that minimum with their blocking and carried load. Inputs are limited to 0.01-1,000 erlangs, 1-1,500 trunks and a 0.01-50% target. The calculation is a planning estimate that assumes one overflow-free group and runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Erlang B blocking formula: B(0) = 1 and B(n) = A x B(n-1) / (n + A x B(n-1)), the fraction of calls refused when blocked calls are cleared
Erlang as a unit of traffic intensity: one erlang is one circuit occupied for the whole hour, so busy-hour call attempts x mean holding time / 3600 gives the load
